title: Light cards — a room's place and who is there, with no reader and no socket

tasks.title: The stream summary carries heRef and the source's title
End to end — no sockets in a feed of live cards, and the visual checks

acs.text: WHEN the feed shows a room or a shiur THE SYSTEM SHALL render it as an `<article>` labelled by its heading, whose heading holds the card's only link, stretched over the whole card; the link's `href` is the room's lobby (`/social/r/<id>`) or the shiur's page (`/social/s/<id>`), and a plain click on a room that is not live, or on a shiur, goes there through social's router (R15).
scenarios: A card is an article with one stretched link

acs.text: WHEN a card shows status THE SYSTEM SHALL take it from the feed (the server's status read) and say it in words — "Live", the number of people learning, "Not live now", or the shiur's start time — with any icon or colour only decorative (`aria-hidden`), and the ref in the interface language (`heRef` in Hebrew when known) with `lang` and `dir`.
scenarios: Status in words, ref in the interface language

acs.text: WHEN the feed shows any number of live cards and nobody presses one THE SYSTEM SHALL open no WebSocket and mount no reader; a test counts sockets through the test relay (component) and Playwright's `websocket` events (end to end).
scenarios: A feed of live cards opens no sockets

acs.text: WHEN a publisher's stream is published THE SYSTEM SHALL carry `social.summary = {ref, heRef, title}`, where `heRef` and `title` come from the public text API's answer for that ref (null until it has answered, then published without waiting for the next move); the relay's status read and the server's status carry `heRef`.
scenarios: The stream's summary carries the Hebrew ref

acs.text: Cards and the feed page are checked visually in English, Hebrew and dark on the harness (Playwright screenshots of the feed), and use only the reader's design tokens.
